title: Mirabel and the Contact
premise: Lior Voss, a whistle-blower who has survived four years under four identities, discovers her safe house listed online with interior photos — proof that someone knows exactly who and where she is. The listing's metadata points to a shell company tied to the defense contractor she exposed, and to a scheduled 'gas leak' that will destroy the apartment block housing the journalist who holds her only backup evidence. Forced out of hiding, Lior assembles an unlikely crew — a retired forger, the realtor who unknowingly listed her home, and the estranged daughter of her former handler — and races to expose the attack before it happens. In the end, Lior chooses truth over survival: she testifies publicly under her real name, sacrificing the anonymity that kept her alive, but gains a family that knows all four of her names and stays anyway.
about_author: Kestrel Delacroix is the pen name of a former investigative researcher who spent a decade embedded with whistle-blower protection networks before turning to fiction. She writes paranoid, character-driven thrillers from an undisclosed location she claims is 'somewhere with good coffee and bad cell service.'

chapters.title: The House That Wasn't Empty
chapters.summary: Lior Voss's POV. Scrolling real estate listings for a decoy property, she freezes: her safe house, photographed from inside — her toothbrush, her go-bag's outline under the bed. The emotional beat is cold vertigo; the life she built to be invisible has been cataloged and put on display for someone to buy.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Bag
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, flashing between identities. She burns her current name, moves the go-bag, and traces the listing to Halcyon Meridian Holdings — the shell network of Corvane Defense, the contractor she exposed four years ago. Beat: controlled panic sharpening into purpose; she realizes she wasn't found, she was flushed.

chapters.title: The Realtor Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Dana Okonkwo (the realtor) POV. Lior confronts Dana, expecting a hired spy; instead she finds a single mother who was fed the listing by a client she never met. Dana, terrified but stubborn, offers her access to the listing's digital trail. Beat: reluctant alliance, first crack in Lior's solitude.

chapters.title: Metadata and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lior's POV with Dana assisting. The listing's upload metadata reveals a scheduled maintenance permit for the building where journalist Amara Chen — holder of Lior's backup evidence — lives: an 'inspection' dated in nine days, filed by Corvane's facilities arm. Beat: dread hardening into a deadline; the attack will look like a gas leak.

chapters.title: The Forger's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She seeks out Elias Brandt, the retired document forger who built her second identity, now running a bakery and pretending his past is flour and yeast. He refuses, then relents when he sees the photos of her safe house. Beat: found family begins forming — the man who made her names chooses to stand behind one of them.

chapters.title: The Handler's Daughter
chapters.summary: Mara Ilves POV. Mara, daughter of Lior's former intelligence handler, has spent years resenting the woman her father died protecting. She's been tracking the same shell company for her own reasons. She finds Lior first, gun drawn, and instead of a bullet offers a shared enemy. Beat: hostility curdling into wary partnership; loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: What the Leak Is Really For
chapters.summary: Group POV, braided. The team discovers the gas leak is cover for destroying Corvane's off-books server archive — and Amara Chen is collateral, not the target. Elias forges inspection credentials to get the team inside the building's maintenance network. Beat: rising dread and team cohesion; the plan is built on trust none of them fully has yet.

chapters.title: Nine Days Becomes Two
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A Corvane fixer, the man who once trained her tradecraft, corners her in a parking garage — not to kill her, but to offer her old name back if she walks away. She refuses, and realizes the schedule has moved up. Beat: betrayal and temptation; the past offers comfort at the price of everyone she's come to love.

chapters.title: The Night of the Inspection
chapters.summary: Full-cast POV rotation. The team infiltrates the building on the rescheduled night: Dana evacuates tenants under a forged gas-company order, Mara confronts the fixer, Elias jams the ignition system, and Lior reaches Amara's apartment to copy the archive as the pressure valves begin to fail. Beat: white-knuckle climax; every loyalty tested under fire.

chapters.title: The Name I Answer To
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The attack is exposed; Corvane's archive goes public under Amara's byline, and the fixer is arrested. Lior stands before a parliamentary inquiry and says her real name aloud for the first time in four years. Beat: resolution and release — she loses her invisibility and gains something rarer: people who know every name she's worn and call her family anyway.
